review_candidates.title: Chief of Staff
review_candidates.description: About the Opportunity An international non-profit organization focused on community-led development and youth leadership seeks an experienced, mission-driven executive to serve as Chief Of Staff. This is an executive leadership role with delegated authority, functioning as the primary deputy and second-in-command to the Chief Executive Officer. The Chief Of Staff leads the organization's internal management and directs the executive leadership team, enabling the CEO to focus on strategic vision, fundraising, partnership development, and Board governance. The role oversees organizational performance, annual planning, operational alignment, and capacity building across multi-country operations. Position Details Employment Type: Full time, exempt Location: United States (Remote, with availability during working hours across Africa) or a regional country office, with regular international travel to program offices Compensation: $240,000 – $260,000 annually, commensurate with experience Benefits: Comprehensive benefits package including health coverage, retirement benefits, and paid time off Reporting Structure Reports directly to the Chief Executive Officer Direct reports include: Chief Operating Officer, Chief Financial Officer, Chief Program Officer, Director of People and Culture, and two Regional Directors Key Responsibilities Second-in-Command to the CEO Serve as the CEO's deputy and operational thought partner, exercising delegated authority to manage internal operations and acting on the CEO's behalf during travel or absence. Maintain organizational clarity and leadership discipline to support executive focus on vision, relationships, resource development, and governance. Prepare and deliver consolidated weekly executive briefings covering operations, finance, programs, development, human resources, and risk. Ensure critical matters brought to the CEO include complete context, viable alternatives, risk assessments, and diverse perspectives, resolving issues at operational levels when feasible. Steward decision-rights frameworks and decision trees, guiding leaders on boundaries of autonomy, cross-functional collaboration, and matters requiring CEO or Board review. Provide objective, constructive feedback and strategic counsel to the CEO. Evaluate and pressure-test high-impact decisions to confirm rigorous analysis, operational viability, and alignment with organizational priorities. Leadership Team Management and Development Direct and facilitate a collaborative executive leadership team accountable for shared goals and organizational performance. Establish performance benchmarks, responsibilities, and decision rights for direct reports, holding leaders accountable for departmental outcomes and team health. Coach senior executives through regular feedback, supporting leadership independence and modeling sustainable work-life balance. Empower functional and regional leaders to design solutions within defined parameters, stepping in directly when performance, compliance, or risk warrants intervention. Identify and eliminate operational bottlenecks, misaligned priorities, and resource constraints across teams. Cultivate a culture of transparency, accountability, proactive communication, and continuous learning. Promote cross-functional and cross-regional alignment so organizational priorities take precedence over departmental interests. Oversee succession planning and leadership development to ensure business continuity across key roles. Direct executive-level hiring processes for CEO approval, and approve country leadership appointments and organizational structural changes. Strategy Execution and Performance Management Partner with the Chief Operating Officer to guide strategic planning initiatives across the global organization. Translate strategic priorities into actionable annual operating plans with defined targets, resource allocations, milestones, and governance checkpoints. Maintain a structured performance rhythm utilizing standardized scorecards reviewed on weekly and quarterly cycles to track progress and mitigate operational risks. Oversee multi-year organizational optimization initiatives to streamline, document, and standardize policies, operating systems, and workflows across central and regional offices. Lead high-priority, cross-cutting strategic initiatives from design through execution and operational handoff. Advance initiatives to strengthen locally led regional leadership, systems, and shared operational services. Program, Operations, Finance, and Risk Oversight Oversee program design, quality, training, and monitoring, evaluation, research, and learning (MERL) through the Chief Program Officer and Regional Directors. Oversee day-to-day administrative operations, IT infrastructure, and shared operational systems through the Chief Operating Officer. Oversee multi-currency budgeting, financial reporting, statutory filings, audits, and financial controls through the Chief Financial Officer; co-present annual operating budgets to the CEO and Board of Directors. Oversee global human resources policy, compensation structures, employee handbooks, and performance management through the Director of People and Culture. Approve organization-wide operational policies (including HR, travel, procurement, and safeguarding) and enterprise system selections, establishing delegation-of-authority matrices and financial decision frameworks in coordination with the CFO. Direct safety, security, and emergency preparedness: maintain incident command structures, approve duty-of-care and evacuation protocols for staff and program participants, conduct scenario trainings, lead crisis response, and escalate severe incidents to executive leadership immediately. Oversee multi-country legal and regulatory compliance in coordination with external legal counsel. Direct internal audit activities to verify compliance with operating standards, prioritizing targeted training and resource allocation to address operational gaps. Required Qualifications 15–20 years of progressive executive leadership experience (such as COO, CEO, Executive Director, Country Director, or an equivalent role) within complex, multi-country, mission-driven organizations. Direct experience living and working in Africa. Demonstrated success establishing and leading organizational headquarters operations (finance, HR, IT, legal, and compliance) across multiple African countries, including implementing internationally benchmarked compensation and HR standards. Strong financial acumen, including multi-entity and multi-currency budgeting, financial forecasting, audit oversight, and executive-level financial reporting. Demonstrated track record of leading senior executives through coaching, influence, and accountability. Demonstrated history of developing leaders, strengthening organizational capacity, and creating sustainable operating rhythms and accountability systems. Proven experience leading volunteer-based or community-led development programs. Demonstrated experience directing crisis response, emergency management, and duty-of-care protocols for staff and participants in high-risk environments, including incident command and scenario training. Fluency in English. Demonstrated alignment with participatory community development, youth leadership, transparency, and accountability. Preferred Qualifications Master of Business Administration (MBA) or equivalent advanced degree. Professional proficiency in French. Experience serving as a primary deputy or second-in-command to an organizational founder. Familiarity with the Peace Corps model or similar international volunteer service frameworks. review_candidates.description: About Us We are EnduroSat! A fast-growing space scale-up at the forefront of satellite innovation, specializing in advanced software-flexible satellites for commercial, governmental, and scientific endeavors. This is more than a job, it`s a mission We are making space universally accessible and redefining the possible We get things done We take ownership of what we do and we work hard to make a difference We are fearless Transpаrancy is our only way forward. We dare to address and resolve issues head-on We learn from our mistakes We deliver, take informed risks, and evolve to achieve our goals. We compare with the best version of ourselves What is the role? We are seeking a highly skilled and detail-oriented Test Engineer to join our engineering team for AIT (Assembly, Integration, and Testing) of satellites. The ideal candidate will specialize in the testing of satellite payloads and spacecraft buses, ensuring the seamless planning and execution of testing satellite modules through fully-integrated satellites. The role will require working closely with cross-functional teams to ensure that all systems meet technical specifications, are integrated correctly, and undergo thorough testing before launch. This role is based in Denver, Colorado, where we are building a high-performing and fast-paced team. The position will be primarily on-site and in person at the office. Some of your daily tasks will also include: Assembly, Integration, and Testing: Lead the testing of spacecraft buses, ensuring that all components work together as designed. Collaborate with payload engineers, bus engineers, and other team members to define interfaces and test requirements. Develop and execute test plans and procedures, ensuring the system meets all performance requirements. Troubleshoot integration and test issues, providing solutions to challenges that arise during the integration and test phases. Ensure all payload and bus test activities adhere to company processes, quality standards, and industry regulations. Develop, implement, and manage test procedures for various satellite subsystems, including payloads, buses, and power systems. Develop and execute test scripts to standardize and automate testing Ensure projects stay on schedule and work cross-functionally to quickly resolve issues that arise across all phases of AIT. Support environmental testing, including thermal/vacuum tests, vibration testing, and electrical performance testing. Documentation and Reporting: Prepare detailed documentation for testing processes, including test plans, test procedures, test reports, and troubleshooting logs. Maintain accurate records of AIT activities, including test results, and communicate progress to senior engineering and program management teams. Provide recommendations for improvements based on test results and lessons learned from integration and testing activities. What do we look for? Bachelor’s degree in Systems Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field (Master’s preferred). 3+ years of experience in systems engineering or AIT roles, with a focus on satellite payload and bus integration. Hands-on experience with satellite payloads, spacecraft buses, and integration/testing procedures. Experience with satellite environmental testing (e.g., thermal vacuum, vibration, EMI/EMC testing) is highly desirable. Proficiency in systems engineering processes, including requirements management, verification, and validation. Familiarity with AIT tools, equipment, and test setups used in satellite integration and test. Excellent communication skills, both verbal and written, to effectively report on test results, document issues, and communicate with various teams. Willingness to travel occasionally in the US and internationally. Based in the Denver area or willing to relocate. US citizen or US permanent resident. How to Stand Out: Previous experience in project execution applying ECSS standards Demonstrated hands-on experience testing satellite platforms System modeling and simulation tools such as Matlab, Simulink and Python Knowledge of cloud-based architectures Knowledge of security architectures and standards applicable to space systems. Knowledge of satellite onboard processing and image processing and the potential use of AI algorithms for edge computing. What do we offer? Health insurance coverage Matching 401k plan Generous team performance-based bonus Collaboration with EnduroSat offices in Sofia, Berlin, and Toulouse, with occasional international travel Salary range: $120,000 - $150,000 per year. The state of Colorado requires listing salary details. The salary will likely be within this range although it may differ based on experience level or other factors. Why EnduroSat? Fast-paced and delivery-focused culture We work with well-defined quarterly based objectives, that allow us to fast-track the progression of our work and improve as we go Tough engineering challenges & hard-core R&D You will be able to work on unique space technology and build next-gen innovations, while mentored by world-recognized space experts Constant learning and progression Own your personal growth by navigating through our career progression framework and educational programs Chance to join our space educational program Meet international space experts and improve your knowledge and skillset with our hands-on educational program At EnduroSat, we embrace diversity and strive to create an inclusive environment where everyone is treated with fairness and respect.
